sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_ui_page"><sys_ui_page action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><category>general</category><client_script/><description>COMMAND dashboards surface</description><direct>false</direct><endpoint>x_2185255_command_cmd_dashboard.do</endpoint><html><![CDATA[<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?>
<j:jelly trim="false" xmlns:j="jelly:core" xmlns:g="glide" xmlns:j2="null" xmlns:g2="null">

<!--
  COMMAND dashboard surface.

  Three platform constraints shape this file, all measured on this instance and
  all silent when violated.

  1. Client JavaScript is never inline. Jelly evaluates script bodies, and a
     CDATA-wrapped one makes the platform serve the whole page as zero bytes with
     HTTP 200 and nothing in any log. So the renderer is a UI Script loaded by src,
     with a content hash on the URL because .jsdbx is cached hard.

  2. The page does not fetch its own data. An XHR from a logged-in session to a
     Scripted REST endpoint never returns here, and the Table API behaves the same
     way from the same context. Everything is computed in g:evaluate below and
     embedded, which costs one round trip and no waterfall.

  3. The payload travels as base64. Jelly evaluates ${...} and $[...] inside
     attributes and text, and a JSON payload carries field labels and record values
     from the instance, any of which could contain those sequences. Base64 has no
     $, no braces and no quotes, so it cannot be evaluated, cannot break the XML,
     and cannot be mangled by HTML escaping. The renderer decodes it as UTF-8.
-->

<g:evaluate var="jvar_b64" jelly="true">
  var table = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('table') || 'incident');

  /* Coerced to a JavaScript string before anything is done to it, and this is
     load-bearing rather than tidiness. RP.getParameterValue returns a
     java.lang.String, so `.split('|')` binds to Java's split(regex), not
     JavaScript's split(literal) -- and in a regex `|` is alternation, so Java
     splits on the empty pattern and returns one element per character.
     "category:software" parsed into sixteen drill levels, one per letter, each
     read as a field name, and the record-list query built from them was
     "cISEMPTY^aISEMPTY^tISEMPTY". Same trap as the java.lang.String `.length`
     one in CmdData, in a different disguise. */
  var rawPath = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('path') || '');

  /* The drill path travels in the URL as field:key|field:key, so a drill state is
     shareable and the browser back button reverses it for free. */
  var path = [];
  if (rawPath) {
    var segs = rawPath.split('|');
    for (var i = 0; i < segs.length; i++) {
      var bits = segs[i].split(':');
      if (!bits[0]) continue;
      path.push({
        field: decodeURIComponent(bits[0]),
        key: bits.length > 1 ? decodeURIComponent(bits[1]) : ''
      });
    }
  }

  /* The time window, as a slicer in the URL.
     Clamped to a declared set rather than trusted, because it reaches a query
     builder and an arbitrary number here would let a link ask for a thousand
     buckets. Twelve is the default and the window a leader reads by habit. */
  var months = parseInt(RP.getParameterValue('months'), 10);
  var allowed = [3, 6, 12, 24];
  var ok = false;
  for (var w = 0; w < allowed.length; w++) if (allowed[w] === months) ok = true;
  if (!ok) months = 12;

  /* A saved report, rather than a bare table, when one is named.

     Same page, same renderer, same drill mechanics. The report supplies the
     table and the base filter and the page is otherwise identical, which is the
     point: a converted report is not a separate surface to build or to keep
     working. Coerced to a JavaScript string for the same reason `path` is. */
  var reportId = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('report') || '');

  /* Chosen chart forms, as field:form pairs, so a customised view is a link.
     No persistence and no preference record: the state is the URL, which means
     it is shareable, bookmarkable and reversed by the back button for free, and
     it costs nothing to store or to invalidate. Coerced to a JavaScript string
     before splitting, for the same java.lang.String reason `path` is.

     Not validated here beyond shape. A form name that this data cannot honestly
     carry is dropped by CmdPayload against the alternatives it computed for that
     panel, which is the same list the on-screen control offers. Validating in two
     places would let the two disagree. */
  /* Which dimension's breakdown to force onto the page with no filter applied.
     Set by the "Where you can go next" and "Drill into X" links, which only
     ever meant "show me this field," never "filter to a value" -- see the
     comment in CmdPayload.dashboard next to opts.focus for why that used to be
     conflated with a real drill step. Coerced to a JavaScript string for the
     same java.lang.String reason `path` is; validated against the table's own
     dimensions downstream, not here. */
  var focus = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('focus') || '');

  var rawForms = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('forms') || '');
  var forms = {};
  if (rawForms) {
    var fsegs = rawForms.split('|');
    for (var fi = 0; fi < fsegs.length; fi++) {
      var fbits = fsegs[fi].split(':');
      if (fbits.length < 2 || !fbits[0]) continue;
      forms[decodeURIComponent(fbits[0])] = decodeURIComponent(fbits[1]);
    }
  }

  /* A portfolio of the client's CEO Dashboard, redrawn. Its measures are PA
     indicators rather than a table and a filter, so it is built by CmdCeo -- but
     what it produces is an ordinary payload, and everything below this point
     treats it as one. */
  var portfolio = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('portfolio') || '');

  /* One measure of a portfolio, opened as a subject in our own surface. Only the
     indicator's id travels here; its query is re-resolved server-side from
     pa_indicators, so no encoded query ever arrives from a browser. */
  var measure = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('measure') || '');

  /* Workspace context, from the "Analyse in COMMAND" list action. Coerced to
     JavaScript strings for the same java.lang.String reason `path` is, and not
     otherwise interpreted here: CmdWorkspace.context is the one place that
     decides what of this the engine may use. `embed` only changes chrome. */
  var wsMode = ('' + (RP.getParameterValue('ws') || '')) === '1';
  var wq = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('wq') || '');
  var wgroup = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('wgroup') || '');
  var wsel = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('wsel') || '');
  var wlist = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('wlist') || '');
  var wrec = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('wrec') || '');
  var wtitle = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('wtitle') || '');
  var embed = ('' + (RP.getParameterValue('embed') || '')) === '1';

  /* A saved report opened from a workspace list of reports (row menu, or one
     report ticked). What the viewer means is "analyse this report", not
     "analyse the table of report definitions", so it becomes the ordinary
     converted-report page -- the report's own table and saved filter, re-read
     from sys_report server-side, never from the URL. */
  var reportFromList = false;
  var wsReportRefusal = '';
  if (wsMode) {
    if (table === 'sys_report') {
      var rid = /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/.test(wrec) ? wrec : (/^[0-9a-f]{32}$/.test(wsel) ? wsel : '');
      if (rid) {
        reportId = rid;
        wsMode = false;
        reportFromList = true;
      } else {
        wsReportRefusal = 'To analyse a saved report, open its row menu and choose ' +
          'Analyse in COMMAND, or tick exactly one report and use the header button.';
      }
    }
  }

  var out;
  try {
    var builder = new CmdPayload();
    if (portfolio || measure) {
      var ceo = new CmdCeo(builder.data, builder.meta, builder.drill);
      if (!ceo.available()) {
        throw 'no CEO dashboard source is configured on this instance. ' +
              'Set the property ' + CmdCeo.SOURCE_PROPERTY + ' to the table ' +
              'holding the slot configuration.';
      }
      if (measure) {
        /* The CEO Dashboard's period, when the measure was opened from one of its
           cards, so the analysis counts the same rows as the card did. Checked
           against the board's own declared periods, never trusted. */
        var ceoPeriod = '' + (RP.getParameterValue('period') || '');
        var P = null;
        if (ceoPeriod) {
          if (typeof CmdCeoBoard !== 'undefined') P = CmdCeoBoard.periodOf(ceoPeriod);
        }
        out = ceo.measure(builder, measure, path,
                          { months: months, forms: forms, focus: focus,
                            portfolio: portfolio,
                            periodDays: P ? P.days : 0,
                            periodLabel: P ? P.label : '',
                            periodKey: P ? P.key : '' });
        if (!out) {
          throw 'that measure could not be resolved to a table and a filter, ' +
                'so there is nothing to analyse.';
        }
      } else {
        out = ceo.portfolio(portfolio, { months: months });
      }
      out.window = { months: months, allowed: allowed };
      out.forms = forms;
    } else if (wsReportRefusal) {
      out = { error: wsReportRefusal, workspace: { title: wtitle },
              subject: { table: table, label: table, rows: 0 },
              panels: [], path: [], notes: [], drill: { atMax: true, options: [] } };
    } else if (wsMode) {
      /* Opened from a workspace list by "Analyse in COMMAND". The list's own
         query, grouping, selection and title arrive here as URL parameters and
         go through CmdWorkspace before the engine sees any of them -- see the
         class comment for the two ways a URL query differs from a report's
         saved filter. A refused context is shown as a refusal and analyses
         nothing; it never falls back to the whole table. */
      var wsp = new CmdWorkspace();
      var wctx = wsp.context(table, {
        query: wq, list: wlist, group: wgroup, selected: wsel, title: wtitle });
      if (!wctx.ok) {
        out = { error: wctx.error,
                subject: { table: table, label: table, rows: 0 },
                panels: [], path: [], notes: [], drill: { atMax: true, options: [] } };
      } else {
        /* The grouped column leads only at the top level. Once the viewer has
           drilled, the path is the question and forcing the list's grouping
           back onto every level would redraw a breakdown of one value. */
        out = builder.dashboard(table, path, {
          months: months, forms: forms,
          focus: focus || (path.length ? '' : wctx.focus),
          baseQuery: wctx.query });
      }
      var wdims = wctx.ok ? builder.meta.dimensions(table) : [];
      out.workspace = {
        fields: wsp.fieldChoices(wdims, wctx.columns, wctx.focus),
        record: wrec ? wsp.recordContext(table, wrec, wdims, wctx.columns) : null,
        title: wctx.title,
        listQuery: wctx.listQuery,
        list: wctx.list,
        selected: wctx.selectedIds.join(','),
        group: wctx.focus,
        clauses: wctx.clauses,
        notes: wctx.notes
      };
    } else if (reportId) {
      var conv = new CmdReport(builder.data, builder.meta, builder.form);
      out = conv.convert(builder, reportId, path, { months: months, forms: forms, focus: focus });
    } else {
      out = builder.dashboard(table, path, { months: months, forms: forms, focus: focus });
    }
    out.window = { months: months, allowed: allowed };
    out.forms = forms;
  } catch (e) {
    out = { error: 'The dashboard could not be built: ' + e,
            subject: { table: table, label: table, rows: 0 },
            panels: [], path: [], notes: [], drill: { atMax: true, options: [] } };
  }
  out.embed = embed;
  /* The two engines offer different base64 encoders and neither has both.
     Measured on dev390988: in global, GlideStringUtil.base64Encode works and
     typeof gs.base64Encode is 'undefined'; inside a scoped application it is the
     other way round and GlideStringUtil is not a usable object there. Feature
     detected rather than branched on scope, so one page source deploys to both
     and neither deployment carries a code path the other never runs. */
  var payloadJson = JSON.stringify(out);
  var encoded = (typeof gs.base64Encode === 'function')
      ? gs.base64Encode(payloadJson)
      : GlideStringUtil.base64Encode(payloadJson);
  encoded;
</g:evaluate>

<style>
/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   COMMAND. Light-first, because ServiceNow runs light and this has to belong
   inside the platform rather than visit it.

   Tokens are the validated light-theme steps from design/command-brand-kit.html:
   categorical hues re-stepped for a white surface and re-validated there against
   the OKLab lightness band, the chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation and
   the WCAG contrast floor. They are not a tint of the dark theme.
   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
:root{
  --void:#F3F5F8; --ground:#F7F9FB; --surface:#FFFFFF;
  --surface-2:#F8FAFC; --surface-3:#EDF0F5;
  --edge:rgba(16,22,32,.10); --edge-2:rgba(16,22,32,.17); --edge-lit:rgba(16,22,32,.28);
  --ink-1:#10161F; --ink-2:#475364; --ink-3:#6B778A; --ink-4:#99A3B3;
  --grid:rgba(16,22,32,.07); --baseline:rgba(16,22,32,.18);

  /* categorical, fixed order, never cycled */
  --c1:#008C9E; --c2:#A5741F; --c3:#6355C8;
  --c4:#C24438; --c5:#1B8A67; --c6:#9A4B90; --c-other:#7A8394;

  /* sequential runs light to dark on a white ground */
  --q1:#E2F2F5; --q2:#C2E4EA; --q3:#93CFDA;
  --q4:#55B0C0; --q5:#008C9E; --q6:#006B7A; --q7:#00505C;

  --ok:#167C4F; --warn:#8A6410; --crit:#C0272E;
  --ok-wash:rgba(22,124,79,.10); --warn-wash:rgba(138,100,16,.11);
  --crit-wash:rgba(192,39,46,.10);

  /* The empty step. A heatmap cell with no records is not the lightest step of
     the ramp -- that would read as "a few" -- it is off the ramp entirely. */
  --q0:#F0F3F7;

  /* Diverging pair, for the one encoding in this product that carries polarity
     rather than identity: a waterfall step and a variance column. Deliberately
     NOT the status tokens. Status means good/bad, which is a judgement nobody on
     this engagement has defined for a change in volume -- more incidents may be
     better reporting -- so these say up and down and nothing more. */
  --up:#2C6FB5; --down:#B5562C;

  --fill-area:.30;

  --display:"Space Grotesk", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
  --sans:-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
  --mono:"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace;
  --ease-out:cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1);
}

/* The platform wraps UI Pages in its own chrome, so everything is scoped under
   the mount rather than applied to body. Nothing here can leak into the nav. */
#cmd-wrap, #cmd-wrap *, #cmd-wrap *::before, #cmd-wrap *::after{box-sizing:border-box}
#cmd-wrap{
  background:var(--void); color:var(--ink-1);
  font-family:var(--sans); font-size:14px; line-height:1.6;
  -webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;
  padding:28px 28px 64px; min-height:100vh;
}
#cmd-wrap a{color:inherit; text-decoration:none}

.d2{font-family:var(--display); font-size:clamp(24px,3vw,34px); line-height:1.08;
  letter-spacing:-.03em; font-weight:600; margin:6px 0 0}
.h3{font-family:var(--display); font-size:15px; line-height:1.3;
  letter-spacing:-.012em; font-weight:600; margin-bottom:6px}
.sm{font-size:12.5px; line-height:1.56; color:var(--ink-2); margin:0 0 12px}
.mono{font-family:var(--mono)}

/* ── header ── */
.app-h{display:flex; align-items:flex-start; justify-content:space-between;
  gap:20px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:22px}
.app-h-r{display:flex; align-items:center; gap:9px; flex-wrap:wrap}
.crumb{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.13em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-3); display:flex; gap:8px;
  align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap}
.crumb a{color:var(--ink-3); border-bottom:1px solid transparent}
.crumb a:hover{color:var(--ink-1); border-bottom-color:var(--edge-2)}
.crumb .sep{color:var(--ink-4)}
.crumb .now{color:var(--ink-1); font-weight:600}
.sub{display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; margin-top:7px;
  font-size:12.5px; color:var(--ink-3)}
.sub .dot{color:var(--ink-4)}

.btn{font-size:12.5px; font-weight:500; padding:7px 13px; border-radius:7px;
  border:1px solid var(--edge-2); cursor:pointer; color:var(--ink-1);
  background:linear-gradient(180deg,#FFFFFF,#F5F7FA);
  display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:7px; white-space:nowrap;
  transition:border-color .18s var(--ease-out), background .18s var(--ease-out)}
.btn:hover{border-color:var(--edge-lit); background:linear-gradient(180deg,#FFFFFF,#EDF1F6)}

.chip{display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; font-family:var(--mono);
  font-size:9.5px; font-weight:500; letter-spacing:.11em; text-transform:uppercase;
  padding:5px 9px; border-radius:5px; border:1px solid var(--edge);
  color:var(--ink-2); background:rgba(16,22,32,.03); white-space:nowrap}
.chip.sm{font-size:9px; padding:3px 7px}
.chip .dot{width:5px; height:5px; border-radius:50%; background:currentColor; flex:none}
.chip.ok{color:var(--ok); border-color:rgba(22,124,79,.3); background:var(--ok-wash)}
.chip.warn{color:var(--warn); border-color:rgba(138,100,16,.3); background:var(--warn-wash)}
.chip.crit{color:var(--crit); border-color:rgba(192,39,46,.3); background:var(--crit-wash)}

/* ── panel: the core material ── */
.panel{position:relative; border-radius:13px; min-width:0;
  background:linear-gradient(180deg,#FFFFFF,#FCFDFE);
  box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.9), 0 1px 2px rgba(16,22,32,.05),
             0 12px 28px -18px rgba(16,22,32,.22)}
.panel::before{content:""; position:absolute; inset:0; border-radius:inherit;
  padding:1px; pointer-events:none;
  background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(16,22,32,.13), rgba(16,22,32,.06));
  -webkit-mask:linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#000 0 0);
  -webkit-mask-composite:xor; mask-composite:exclude}
.panel > *{position:relative}
.pad{padding:20px}

.grid-panels{display:grid; gap:14px; grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))}
.grid-panels .span2{grid-column:span 2}

/* ── skeleton ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   The client's own words: "report design outcome skeleton". There is nothing
   this can swap into once real content arrives -- the payload is embedded in
   the initial HTML server-side (see cmd_dashboard.xhtml's g:evaluate), so by
   the time this page's own JS runs, the data is already sitting in the DOM.
   The entire wait a viewer feels is server build time that happens before the
   browser receives a single byte of the response -- measured elsewhere in this
   engagement at 2 to 7+ seconds depending on table and persona -- and no
   partial response or safe client fetch exists to paint into during it (an
   XHR from a logged-in session on this instance was measured never to
   return). So this paints on the PAGE BEING LEFT, the instant a link to
   another COMMAND page is clicked, shaped like the page that is coming --
   header, KPI row, chart grid for a dashboard; header and a card grid for the
   catalog -- then hands off to the browser's own navigation. No network call,
   no swap-in, nothing that could hang: it is a still frame painted from
   knowledge already on the page, held for exactly as long as the real
   response takes, then replaced by it. */
.skel-block{border-radius:8px; background:var(--surface-3);
  position:relative; overflow:hidden}
.skel-block::after{content:''; position:absolute; inset:0;
  background:linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, var(--edge-lit), transparent);
  animation:skel-sweep 1.6s ease-in-out infinite}
@keyframes skel-sweep{
  from{transform:translateX(-100%)} to{transform:translateX(100%)}
}
.skel-h1{height:13px; width:120px; margin-bottom:14px}
.skel-h2{height:30px; width:60%; max-width:340px; margin-bottom:6px}
.skel-h3{height:13px; width:40%; max-width:220px}
.skel-kpis{display:flex; gap:14px; margin:24px 0}
.skel-kpi{flex:1; height:96px}
.skel-panel{height:280px}
.skel-title{height:14px; width:45%; margin-bottom:8px}
.skel-sub{height:10px; width:70%}
.skel-panel-h{padding:15px}
.skel-cards{display:grid; gap:14px; grid-template-columns:repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr))}
.skel-card{height:150px}
@media (max-width:900px){
  .skel-kpis{flex-direction:column}
  .grid-panels, .skel-cards{grid-template-columns:1fr}
}

.cp{display:flex; flex-direction:column; padding:18px 18px 15px}
.cp-h{display:flex; align-items:flex-start; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px}
.cp-t{font-family:var(--display); font-size:14px; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-.014em}
.cp-s{font-size:11.5px; color:var(--ink-3); margin-top:4px; line-height:1.45}
.cp-m{display:flex; gap:6px; flex:none; padding-top:2px}
.form-tag{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9px; letter-spacing:.11em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-3); border:1px solid var(--edge);
  border-radius:4px; padding:3px 6px; white-space:nowrap}
.cp-b{margin-top:16px; flex:1; min-height:0}
.cp.focus{box-shadow:0 0 0 1.5px var(--c1) inset}
.cp-focus-tag{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9px; letter-spacing:.11em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--c1); margin-top:6px}
.cp-f{margin-top:14px; padding-top:12px; border-top:1px solid var(--edge);
  display:flex; gap:16px; flex-wrap:wrap; align-items:center}
.drill-link{font-size:12px; font-weight:500; color:var(--c1);
  border-bottom:1px solid transparent}
.drill-link:hover{border-bottom-color:var(--c1)}
.drill-link.muted{color:var(--ink-3)}
.drill-link.muted:hover{color:var(--ink-1); border-bottom-color:var(--edge-2)}

.cavs{margin-top:12px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:6px}
.cav{font-size:11.5px; line-height:1.5; color:var(--ink-2);
  border-left:0; padding:8px 10px; border-radius:6px; background:var(--surface-3)}
.cav.warn{color:var(--warn); background:var(--warn-wash)}

.note{font-size:12.5px; line-height:1.55; color:var(--ink-2);
  border:1px solid var(--edge); border-radius:9px; padding:14px 16px;
  background:var(--surface); margin-top:14px}

/* ── charts ── */
svg.ch{display:block; width:100%; height:auto; overflow:visible}
svg.ch .gl{stroke:var(--grid); stroke-width:1}
svg.ch .bl{stroke:var(--baseline); stroke-width:1}
svg.ch .tk{fill:var(--ink-3); font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9.5px; letter-spacing:.05em}
svg.ch .ct{fill:var(--ink-2); font-family:var(--sans); font-size:11.5px}
svg.ch .ctOn{fill:#FFFFFF; font-family:var(--sans); font-size:11.5px}
svg.ch .vl{fill:var(--ink-1); font-family:var(--display); font-size:11.5px;
  font-weight:600; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
svg.ch .vlOn{fill:#FFFFFF; font-family:var(--display); font-size:11.5px;
  font-weight:600; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
svg.ch .big{fill:var(--ink-1); font-family:var(--display); font-size:30px;
  font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-.035em; font-variant-numeric:lining-nums}
svg.ch .huge{fill:var(--ink-1); font-family:var(--display); font-size:46px;
  font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-.04em; font-variant-numeric:lining-nums}

/* ── tables ── */
.tbl-wrap{overflow-x:auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch}
.tbl{width:100%; border-collapse:collapse; font-size:12.5px;
  font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums lining-nums}
.tbl th{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9px; font-weight:500; letter-spacing:.14em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-3); text-align:right;
  padding:0 12px 9px 0; border-bottom:1px solid var(--edge-2); white-space:nowrap}
.tbl th.l{text-align:left}
.tbl td{padding:9px 12px 9px 0; border-bottom:1px solid var(--edge);
  text-align:right; color:var(--ink-2); white-space:nowrap}
.tbl td.l{text-align:left; color:var(--ink-1)}
.tbl tr:hover td{background:rgba(16,22,32,.02)}
.tbl .vr{color:var(--ink-3); margin-left:9px; font-size:11.5px; white-space:normal}

/* ── drill panel ── */
.drill-list{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:1px; border-radius:9px;
  overflow:hidden; border:1px solid var(--edge); background:var(--edge)}
.drill-row{display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between;
  gap:14px; padding:12px 14px; background:var(--surface);
  transition:background .18s var(--ease-out)}
.drill-row:hover{background:var(--surface-2)}
.drill-row.off{background:var(--surface-3); cursor:default}
.drill-row.off:hover{background:var(--surface-3)}
.drill-l{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:3px; min-width:0}
.drill-n{font-family:var(--display); font-size:13px; font-weight:600}
.drill-r{font-size:11.5px; color:var(--ink-3)}
.drill-row.off .drill-n{color:var(--ink-3)}
.drill-meta{flex:none}

/* ── catalog ── */
.area-h{display:flex; align-items:baseline; gap:12px; margin:26px 0 12px}
.area-n{font-family:var(--display); font-size:17px; font-weight:600;
  letter-spacing:-.02em}
.area-c{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9.5px; letter-spacing:.13em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-3)}
.cards{display:grid; gap:12px; grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(262px,1fr))}
.card{border-radius:12px; overflow:hidden; cursor:pointer; display:flex;
  flex-direction:column; border:1px solid var(--edge);
  background:linear-gradient(180deg,#FFFFFF,#FBFCFE);
  box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(16,22,32,.04);
  transition:transform .26s var(--ease-out), box-shadow .26s var(--ease-out),
             border-color .26s var(--ease-out)}
.card:hover{transform:translateY(-2px); border-color:var(--edge-lit);
  box-shadow:0 14px 32px -18px rgba(16,22,32,.3)}
.card-b{padding:15px 16px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:6px; flex:1}
.card-n{font-family:var(--display); font-size:14px; font-weight:600;
  letter-spacing:-.014em; line-height:1.3}
.card-d{font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-3); line-height:1.45}
.card-f{display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:9px;
  margin-top:auto; padding-top:8px; font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9px;
  letter-spacing:.1em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-4)}


/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   Dark. A selected counterpart, not an inversion.
   Its own steps from the same hues, validated against its own #0D1117 surface.
   Three things genuinely flip and are therefore defined twice rather than
   computed: the sequential ramp direction, because on dark brightness is
   magnitude and on light darkness is; the emphasis step per hue, which goes
   lighter on dark and darker on light; and text sitting on a high sequential
   step. Getting the first of those backwards is the commonest dark-mode
   heatmap bug.
   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"]{
  color-scheme:dark;
  --void:#06080B; --ground:#0A0D12; --surface:#0D1117;
  --surface-2:#121924; --surface-3:#18202D;
  --edge:rgba(255,255,255,.08); --edge-2:rgba(255,255,255,.14); --edge-lit:rgba(255,255,255,.22);
  --ink-1:#E8EDF5; --ink-2:#98A5BA; --ink-3:#606E86; --ink-4:#3B4657;
  --grid:rgba(255,255,255,.06); --baseline:rgba(255,255,255,.13);

  --c1:#16A5BA; --c2:#B8842A; --c3:#7A6DE0;
  --c4:#D8544A; --c5:#2AA47E; --c6:#B25FA8; --c-other:#5A6472;

  /* sequential runs dark to bright here, the inverse of the light theme */
  --q1:#0E252C; --q2:#103A46; --q3:#125264;
  --q4:#146D82; --q5:#16A5BA; --q6:#2AC8DC; --q7:#5EE4F2;

  --ok:#2FBF7F; --warn:#D9A62E; --crit:#FF4C5B;
  --ok-wash:rgba(47,191,127,.13); --warn-wash:rgba(217,166,46,.13);
  --crit-wash:rgba(255,76,91,.13);

  --q0:#0F151E;
  --up:#5A9BE0; --down:#E0895A;

  --fill-area:.38;
}
/* Panels invert their material: on dark the top highlight does the work that the
   hairline and shadow do on light. */
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .panel{
  background:linear-gradient(180deg,#141C27 0%, #0C1118 58%, #0A0E14 100%);
  box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.065), 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.55),
             0 16px 40px -20px rgba(0,0,0,.85)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .panel::before{
  background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,.18), rgba(255,255,255,.03))}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .btn{
  background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,.055), rgba(255,255,255,.012))}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .btn:hover{
  background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,.09), rgba(255,255,255,.025))}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .chip{background:rgba(255,255,255,.03)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .card{
  background:linear-gradient(180deg,#131B26 0%, #0A0E14 100%);
  box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.5)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .card:hover{box-shadow:0 18px 40px -20px rgba(0,0,0,1)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .cav{background:var(--surface-3)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .drill-row{background:var(--surface)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .drill-row:hover{background:var(--surface-2)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .drill-row.off{background:var(--surface-3)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .note{background:var(--surface)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .field{background:rgba(0,0,0,.3)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .tbl tr:hover td{background:rgba(255,255,255,.022)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] svg.ch .ctOn,
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] svg.ch .vlOn{fill:#04161A}

/* ── theme toggle ── */
.seg{display:inline-flex; border:1px solid var(--edge); border-radius:8px; padding:2px;
  background:var(--surface-3); gap:2px}
.seg button{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9.5px; letter-spacing:.09em; padding:5px 10px;
  border:0; border-radius:6px; background:transparent; color:var(--ink-3); cursor:pointer;
  text-transform:uppercase}
.seg button[aria-selected="true"]{color:var(--ink-1); background:var(--surface);
  font-weight:600; box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(16,22,32,.12)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .seg button[aria-selected="true"]{
  box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.07)}

/* ── catalog controls ── */
.cat-bar{display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin:20px 0 6px}
.pager{display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px;
  flex-wrap:wrap; margin:14px 0; padding:10px 12px; border:1px solid var(--edge);
  border-radius:8px; background:var(--surface-2)}
.pager .btn.ghost{opacity:.4; pointer-events:none}
.field{display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; border:1px solid var(--edge-2);
  border-radius:8px; padding:7px 11px; background:var(--surface); min-width:230px}
.field input{border:0; outline:0; background:transparent; color:var(--ink-1);
  font-family:var(--sans); font-size:13px; width:100%}
.field input::placeholder{color:var(--ink-4)}
.filters{display:flex; gap:6px; flex-wrap:wrap}
.fchip{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9.5px; letter-spacing:.1em; text-transform:uppercase;
  padding:6px 10px; border-radius:6px; border:1px solid var(--edge); cursor:pointer;
  color:var(--ink-2); background:var(--surface); white-space:nowrap;
  transition:border-color .16s var(--ease-out), color .16s var(--ease-out)}
.fchip:hover{border-color:var(--edge-lit); color:var(--ink-1)}
.fchip[aria-pressed="true"]{color:var(--ink-1); border-color:var(--edge-lit);
  background:var(--surface-3); font-weight:600}
.cat-count{font-size:12.5px; color:var(--ink-3); margin-left:auto; white-space:nowrap}

/* ── card, restyled: scannable, with a real distribution preview ── */
.card-h{padding:15px 16px 0}
.card-n{font-family:var(--display); font-size:15.5px; font-weight:600;
  letter-spacing:-.016em; line-height:1.25}
.card-sub{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9px; letter-spacing:.1em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-4); margin-top:4px}
.card-stats{display:flex; gap:16px; padding:12px 16px 0; flex-wrap:wrap}
.cs{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:1px}
.cs-v{font-family:var(--display); font-size:17px; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-.02em;
  line-height:1.1; font-variant-numeric:lining-nums}
.cs-l{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:8.5px; letter-spacing:.11em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-4)}
.card-prev{padding:13px 16px 0}
.card-prev-l{font-size:11px; color:var(--ink-3); margin-bottom:6px}
.prev-bar{display:flex; height:7px; border-radius:4px; overflow:hidden; gap:2px;
  background:var(--surface-3)}
.prev-bar i{display:block; height:100%; border-radius:2px}
.prev-keys{display:flex; gap:12px; margin-top:8px; flex-wrap:wrap}
.pk{display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:5px; font-size:11px; color:var(--ink-2)}
.pk i{width:7px; height:7px; border-radius:2px; flex:none}
.card-f{display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:9px;
  margin-top:auto; padding:13px 16px 14px; font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9px;
  letter-spacing:.1em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-4)}
.card-go{color:var(--c1); font-weight:600}
.cards{grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(300px,1fr))}
.empty{padding:26px; text-align:center; color:var(--ink-3); font-size:13px}

/* ── responsive: the panel grid collapses, and wide charts keep their scale ── */
@media(max-width:1000px){
  .grid-panels{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)}
  .grid-panels .span2{grid-column:span 1}
}
@media(max-width:700px){
  #cmd-wrap{padding:16px 14px 44px}
  .cp{padding:14px}
  .pad{padding:15px}
  .cp-b{overflow-x:auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch; scrollbar-width:thin}
  /* A 520-unit viewBox squeezed into 300px renders its 9.5px axis labels at 5px,
     so the chart keeps a floor width and the panel body scrolls instead. */
  .cp-b svg.ch{min-width:430px}
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){
  #cmd-wrap *{transition:none !important; animation:none !important}
}

/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   The analysis layer

   KPI tiles, the report matrix, hover reports, cross-highlighting and the
   filter bar. Everything here is scoped under #cmd-wrap like the rest, with the
   single exception of the tooltip, which is documented at its rule.
   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */

/* ── KPI row ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#cmd-wrap .kpi-row{
  display:grid; gap:12px; margin:0 0 16px;
  grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(230px,100%), 1fr))}
#cmd-wrap .kpi{
  background:var(--surface); border:1px solid var(--edge); border-radius:12px;
  padding:14px 16px 13px; position:relative; overflow:hidden}
#cmd-wrap .kpi-l{
  font-size:11px; letter-spacing:.06em; text-transform:uppercase;
  color:var(--ink-3); margin-bottom:7px}
#cmd-wrap .kpi-v{display:flex; align-items:baseline; gap:9px; flex-wrap:wrap}
#cmd-wrap .kpi-n{
  font-family:var(--display); font-size:31px; line-height:1;
  letter-spacing:-.02em; color:var(--ink-1); font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
#cmd-wrap .kpi-d{
  font-size:12px; font-weight:600; padding:2px 7px; border-radius:20px;
  background:var(--surface-3); color:var(--ink-2);
  font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
/* Direction is carried by an arrow glyph as well as by hue, so the tile is
   readable without colour and in forced-colors mode. */
#cmd-wrap .kpi-d.up{color:var(--up); background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--up) 12%, transparent)}
#cmd-wrap .kpi-d.down{color:var(--down); background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--down) 12%, transparent)}
#cmd-wrap .kpi-s{font-size:11.5px; color:var(--ink-3); margin-top:7px; line-height:1.45}
#cmd-wrap .kpi-c{
  position:absolute; top:10px; right:10px; font-size:9.5px; letter-spacing:.05em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--warn); background:var(--warn-wash);
  padding:2px 6px; border-radius:4px}

/* ── the analytics caption under a trend ─────────────────────────────────── */
#cmd-wrap .cp-an{
  display:flex; gap:8px; align-items:baseline; flex-wrap:wrap;
  margin:10px 0 0; padding-top:10px; border-top:1px solid var(--edge);
  font-size:11.5px; color:var(--ink-3); line-height:1.5}
#cmd-wrap .an-k{
  font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.06em; text-transform:uppercase; font-weight:600;
  color:var(--ink-2); background:var(--surface-3); padding:2px 7px; border-radius:4px}

/* ── the report matrix ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#cmd-wrap table.mx{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
#cmd-wrap table.mx tbody tr:hover{background:var(--surface-2)}
#cmd-wrap table.mx tfoot td{
  border-top:1.5px solid var(--edge-2); font-weight:600; color:var(--ink-1)}
#cmd-wrap .mx-bar{
  height:7px; min-width:56px; background:var(--surface-3); border-radius:4px;
  overflow:hidden}
#cmd-wrap .mx-bar > i{display:block; height:100%; background:var(--c1); border-radius:4px}
#cmd-wrap .spark{width:92px; height:22px; display:block; overflow:visible}
#cmd-wrap td.up{color:var(--up)}
#cmd-wrap td.down{color:var(--down)}

/* ── hover report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
/* The one rule not scoped to the mount. The element is appended to the document
   body on purpose: a tooltip inside the panel is clipped by the panel's own
   overflow, and inside the mobile horizontal-scroll container it scrolls away
   from the mark it belongs to.

   Note for anyone editing this file: an angle bracket in a CSS comment is an open
   tag to the XML parser, because this stylesheet is inlined into a Jelly page.
   Writing the element name in brackets here cost one deploy. */
.cmd-tip{
  position:absolute; z-index:9999; pointer-events:none; opacity:0;
  transform:translateY(3px); transition:opacity .12s var(--ease-out),
  transform .12s var(--ease-out);
  background:var(--surface); color:var(--ink-1);
  border:1px solid var(--edge-2); border-radius:9px; padding:9px 11px;
  box-shadow:0 2px 6px rgba(16,22,32,.09), 0 14px 34px -14px rgba(16,22,32,.35);
  font-family:var(--sans); font-size:12px; line-height:1.55; max-width:290px}
.cmd-tip.on{opacity:1; transform:translateY(0)}
.cmd-tip .tip-h{
  font-weight:650; color:var(--ink-1); margin-bottom:3px;
  font-size:12.5px; letter-spacing:-.005em}
.cmd-tip .tip-r{color:var(--ink-2); font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] .cmd-tip{
  box-shadow:0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.5), 0 14px 34px -14px rgba(0,0,0,.85)}

/* ── cross-highlighting ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#cmd-wrap .hit{cursor:pointer}
#cmd-wrap .hit:focus{outline:2px solid var(--c1); outline-offset:2px}
/* Recede rather than disappear: a dimmed mark still holds its position, so the
   shape of the whole distribution stays readable behind the selection. */
#cmd-wrap .dim{opacity:.17; transition:opacity .15s var(--ease-out)}
#cmd-wrap .lit{opacity:1}
#cmd-wrap tr.lit{background:var(--surface-3)}
#cmd-wrap tr.dim{opacity:.35}

#cmd-wrap .sel-bar{
  display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap;
  margin:0 0 14px; padding:10px 13px; border-radius:10px;
  background:var(--surface-2); border:1px solid var(--edge)}
#cmd-wrap .sel-l{font-weight:600; color:var(--ink-1); font-size:13px}
#cmd-wrap .sel-n{font-size:11.5px; color:var(--ink-3); flex:1 1 220px}

/* ── filter bar ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#cmd-wrap .filter-bar{
  display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin:0 0 15px}
#cmd-wrap .fb-l{
  font-size:10.5px; letter-spacing:.06em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-3)}
#cmd-wrap .fb-chip{
  display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:7px; padding:4px 5px 4px 10px;
  border-radius:20px; background:var(--surface-3); border:1px solid var(--edge);
  font-size:12px}
#cmd-wrap .fb-f{color:var(--ink-3)}
#cmd-wrap .fb-v{color:var(--ink-1); font-weight:600}
#cmd-wrap .fb-x{
  display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center;
  width:17px; height:17px; border-radius:50%; text-decoration:none;
  color:var(--ink-3); background:var(--surface); font-size:13px; line-height:1}
#cmd-wrap .fb-x:hover{color:var(--crit); background:var(--crit-wash)}
#cmd-wrap .fb-clear{font-size:11.5px; color:var(--ink-3); text-decoration:none}
#cmd-wrap .fb-clear:hover{color:var(--ink-1); text-decoration:underline}

/* ── workspace context strip ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
   The list this analysis was opened from, in the list's own terms. Same chip
   grammar as the filter bar below it, with a series-one rule on the left so it
   reads as provenance rather than as another filter to remove. */
#cmd-wrap .ws-strip{
  display:flex; align-items:center; gap:7px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin:-6px 0 16px;
  padding:9px 12px; border-radius:10px; background:var(--surface);
  border:1px solid var(--edge); border-left:3px solid var(--c1)}
#cmd-wrap .ws-l{
  font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.12em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-3); margin-right:4px}
#cmd-wrap .ws-c{
  padding:3px 10px; border-radius:20px; background:var(--surface-3);
  border:1px solid var(--edge); font-size:12px; color:var(--ink-1)}
#cmd-wrap .ws-j{font-size:11px; color:var(--ink-3); text-transform:uppercase;
  letter-spacing:.08em}
#cmd-wrap .ws-g{
  padding:3px 10px; border-radius:20px; font-size:12px; font-weight:600;
  color:var(--c1); border:1px solid var(--c1); background:transparent}

#cmd-wrap .ws-by{display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; margin-left:auto}
#cmd-wrap .ws-by-l{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.12em;
  text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-3)}
#cmd-wrap .ws-by-s{font:inherit; font-size:12.5px; color:var(--ink-1);
  background:var(--surface-3); border:1px solid var(--edge-2); border-radius:8px;
  padding:5px 28px 5px 10px; min-width:200px; cursor:pointer}
#cmd-wrap .ws-by-s:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--c1); outline-offset:2px}
#cmd-wrap .ws-rec{
  display:flex; align-items:center; gap:7px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin:-8px 0 16px;
  padding:9px 12px; border-radius:10px; background:var(--surface);
  border:1px solid var(--edge); border-left:3px solid var(--c2)}
#cmd-wrap .ws-rec-id{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:12.5px; font-weight:600;
  color:var(--c2); text-decoration:underline; text-underline-offset:3px}
#cmd-wrap .ws-f{display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:7px; padding:3px 10px;
  border-radius:20px; background:var(--surface-3); border:1px solid var(--edge);
  font-size:12px; text-decoration:none}
#cmd-wrap .ws-f:hover{border-color:var(--c2)}

/* Inside the workspace modal: the modal already frames the page, so the page's
   own outer padding and full-viewport height would only waste its space. */
.cmd-embed #cmd-wrap{padding:18px 20px 36px; min-height:0}
.cmd-embed #cmd-wrap .app-h{margin-bottom:16px}

/* ── small controls ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#cmd-wrap .seg.sm button{font-size:11px; padding:3px 9px}
#cmd-wrap .btn.sm{font-size:11.5px; padding:4px 11px}
#cmd-wrap .btn.ghost{background:transparent; border-color:var(--edge)}
#cmd-wrap .cp-m{display:flex; align-items:center; gap:9px; flex-wrap:wrap}

/* ── motion ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){
  .cmd-tip, #cmd-wrap .dim{transition:none}
}

/* The window slicer sits in the segmented control, but its items are links
   rather than buttons because each one is a different page. */
#cmd-wrap .seg a{
  display:inline-flex; align-items:center; padding:3px 9px; font-size:11px;
  color:var(--ink-2); text-decoration:none; border-radius:6px;
  font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
#cmd-wrap .seg a[aria-selected="true"]{
  background:var(--surface); color:var(--ink-1); font-weight:600;
  box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(16,22,32,.10)}
:root[data-cmd-theme="dark"] #cmd-wrap .seg a[aria-selected="true"]{
  box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.5)}

/* ── converted report provenance ───────────────────────────────────────────
   Sits between the filter bar and the numbers, because it qualifies every
   number below it. Deliberately quiet: it is evidence, not a banner. */
.prov{margin:0 0 18px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px;
      align-items:flex-start}
.prov-h{display:flex; align-items:baseline; gap:12px; flex-wrap:wrap}
.prov-rows{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:9px; width:100%}
.prov-row{display:flex; align-items:baseline; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap}
.prov-row .sm{color:var(--ink-2); line-height:1.55; flex:1 1 340px; min-width:0}
.prov-forms{display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; flex:0 0 auto}
.prov-forms code{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; letter-spacing:.04em;
                 padding:3px 7px; border:1px solid var(--edge-2); border-radius:5px;
                 color:var(--ink-3); background:var(--surf-2)}
.prov-forms code.now{color:var(--ink-1); border-color:var(--edge-1)}
.prov-forms .sep{color:var(--ink-4)}

/* ── catalog tabs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Two entry points, one surface. Underline rather than a pill because the tab
   row sits directly under a display heading and a second filled shape there
   competes with it. */
.tabs{display:flex; gap:2px; margin:0 0 22px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--edge-2)}
.tab{padding:9px 14px; font-size:12.5px; color:var(--ink-3);
     border-bottom:2px solid transparent; margin-bottom:-1px}
.tab:hover{color:var(--ink-1)}
.tab.now{color:var(--ink-1); font-weight:600; border-bottom-color:var(--accent)}

/* ── saved report list ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   A list, not cards. Cards are for subjects, where a preview chart earns the
   area; a report is a name and a destination, and several hundred of them read
   far faster as dense rows grouped by what they are about. */
.rep-groups{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:26px}
.rep-group-h{display:flex; align-items:baseline; gap:10px; margin-bottom:9px;
             padding-bottom:7px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--edge-2)}
.rep-list{display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(320px,1fr));
          gap:1px; background:var(--edge-2); border:1px solid var(--edge-2);
          border-radius:8px; overflow:hidden}
.rep{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:5px; padding:12px 14px;
     background:var(--surf-1); min-width:0}
.rep:hover{background:var(--surf-2)}
.rep-t{font-size:13px; color:var(--ink-1); line-height:1.4;
       overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.rep-m{display:flex; align-items:center; gap:9px; flex-wrap:wrap;
       font-size:11px; color:var(--ink-3)}
.rep-m code{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.05em;
            color:var(--ink-3)}
.rep-dyn{padding:1px 6px; border:1px solid var(--edge-2); border-radius:999px;
         font-size:10px; color:var(--ink-3)}

/* ── print ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   The browser's print pipeline is also its "save as PDF", so this is the whole
   PDF export. Forced to the light palette regardless of the on-screen theme:
   a dark dashboard printed as-is is a page of ink, and nobody wants the version
   of this file that arrives in an inbox to be the one that empties a cartridge. */
@media print {
  :root, :root[data-theme="dark"] {
    --surf-0:#fff; --surf-1:#fff; --surf-2:#fff;
    --ink-1:#111; --ink-2:#333; --ink-3:#555; --ink-4:#777;
    --edge-1:#bbb; --edge-2:#ddd;
  }
  body{background:#fff}
  .seg, .tabs, .cat-bar, .btn, .fchip, .win, .tip{display:none !important}
  .app-h{border-bottom:1px solid #ddd; padding-bottom:12px}
  /* Panels must not be split across a page break: half a chart on each side of
     a fold is worse than a shorter page. */
  .panel{break-inside:avoid; page-break-inside:avoid; border:1px solid #ddd;
         box-shadow:none}
  .grid-panels{display:block}
  .grid-panels > *{margin:0 0 14px}
  a{text-decoration:none; color:inherit}
  /* The ACL verdict has to survive printing. A number on paper without the
     statement of what it was checked against is the one thing this product
     exists to prevent. */
  .chip{border:1px solid #999 !important; color:#111 !important}
  .prov{border:1px solid #999}
}

/* ── chart form control ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Sits where the form tag used to, because it says the same thing and now
   answers back. Closed it is a label; open it is the argument for the drawing
   plus the alternatives the shape supports and the ones it does not. */
.formsel{position:relative}
.formsel-t{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.11em;
           text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--ink-3); background:none;
           border:1px solid var(--edge-2); border-radius:5px; padding:4px 9px;
           cursor:pointer}
.formsel-t:hover{color:var(--ink-1); border-color:var(--edge-1)}
.formsel.open .formsel-t{color:var(--ink-1); border-color:var(--edge-1)}
.formsel-m{display:none; position:absolute; right:0; top:calc(100% + 6px);
           z-index:40; width:320px; max-width:78vw; padding:12px;
           background:var(--surf-1); border:1px solid var(--edge-1);
           border-radius:9px; box-shadow:0 10px 34px rgba(0,0,0,.16);
           max-height:60vh; overflow-y:auto}
.formsel.open .formsel-m{display:block}
.formsel-h{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:5px; padding-bottom:10px;
           margin-bottom:8px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--edge-2)}
.formsel-h .sm{line-height:1.5}
.formsel-o{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:3px; padding:8px 9px;
           border-radius:6px; margin:0 -3px}
.formsel-o:hover{background:var(--surf-2)}
.formsel-n{font-size:12.5px; color:var(--ink-1)}
.formsel-o .sm, .formsel-x .sm{line-height:1.45; color:var(--ink-3)}
.formsel-r{margin-top:9px; padding-top:9px; border-top:1px solid var(--edge-2);
           display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:7px}
/* Refusals are shown, not hidden, and are deliberately not clickable: the point
   is the reason, not a disabled control inviting a second attempt. */
.formsel-x{display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:3px; opacity:.72}
.formsel-x .formsel-n{color:var(--ink-3); text-decoration:line-through}

/* The empty-slice notice: a drill that landed on nothing. Sized like a panel so
   it sits where the panels would have been, rather than reading as an error
   banner attached to the page. */
.empty-slice { max-width: 640px; }
.empty-slice .h3 { margin-bottom: 6px; }
.empty-acts { display: flex; gap: 8px; margin-top: 14px; flex-wrap: wrap; }

/* A KPI card's own history. Sized to sit under the number without competing with
   it: the value is the statement, the line is the context. */
.kpi-spark { margin-top: 6px; opacity: 0.85; }
.kpi-spark .spark { width: 100%; height: 22px; display: block; }
/* A measure that could not be computed. Muted rather than alarming: on the source
   dashboard the same card shows a confident 0. */
.kpi-n.none { color: var(--ink-3); font-weight: 500; }

/* The record link on a KPI card. Quiet until pointed at: the number is the
   statement, this is the way to check it. */
.kpi-open{
  display:inline-block; margin-top:10px;
  font-family:var(--mono,ui-monospace,monospace); font-size:11px;
  letter-spacing:.04em; text-transform:uppercase;
  color:var(--ink-3); text-decoration:none;
  border-bottom:1px solid transparent; transition:color .12s, border-color .12s;
}
.kpi-open:hover, .kpi-open:focus{ color:var(--c1); border-bottom-color:var(--c1); }
.kpi{ display:flex; flex-direction:column; }

/* One measure of a portfolio, opened as a subject. States what this page is a
   view of and how to leave it, because an analysis you arrived at from a card is
   otherwise indistinguishable from an unexplained filter. */
.measure-bar{
  display:flex; align-items:center; gap:14px; flex-wrap:wrap;
  padding:10px 14px; margin:0 0 18px;
  background:var(--surface-2); border:1px solid var(--edge);
  border-left:2.5px solid var(--c1); border-radius:0 8px 8px 0;
}
.measure-l{ font-family:var(--display,inherit); font-weight:600; color:var(--ink-1); }
.measure-n{ color:var(--ink-3); font-size:12.5px; }

/* The gauge tile. The arc is centred in the space a tile has left after its
   label and above its sub-line, and is capped in width so that a wide tile grows
   the whitespace around it rather than blowing the arc up to a different scale
   from every other mark on the page. */
#cmd-wrap .kpi-gauge{
  display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center;
  margin:2px 0 4px; flex:1 1 auto}
#cmd-wrap .kpi-gauge .ch.gauge{width:100%; max-width:210px; height:auto; display:block}
/* The value inside the arc. Sized in the gauge's own viewBox units so it clears
   the arc's inner radius, rather than inheriting the 46px meant for a viewBox
   two and a half times wider. */
svg.ch.gauge .gval{fill:var(--ink-1); font-family:var(--display); font-size:27px;
  font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-.04em; font-variant-numeric:lining-nums}

</style>

<div id="cmd-wrap">
  <div id="cmd-data" data-view="dashboard" data-b64="${jvar_b64}"></div>
  <div id="cmd-root"></div>
</div>

<!-- Client JavaScript, loaded by g:requires under a content-hashed NAME.
     Two things were tried first and both failed silently, so the reasoning is
     recorded here rather than rediscovered.
     A plain script tag with src and a hash query does not survive: the platform
     sanitises script elements in a UI Page and stores them as an empty pair, so
     the page deploys with no client code at all.
     A fixed name via g:requires does not bust cache: the URL it emits carries the
     platform release stamp, which is identical before and after a deploy, and
     .jsdbx is cached hard. Every browser that had loaded the page once kept
     running the old renderer while the instance served the new one, so the record
     read back byte for byte correct and the screen still showed old code. The
     symptom was panels reporting "no renderer for waterfall yet" against a
     renderer that had already shipped.
     Hashing the asset name changes the path itself, which is the one thing the
     cache cannot ignore. Names are substituted at deploy time and old ones are
     removed. -->
<g:requires name="x_2185255_command.cmd_theme_4cb7076a.jsdbx" includes="true" />
<g:requires name="x_2185255_command.cmd_fonts_96b48415.jsdbx" includes="true" />
<g:requires name="x_2185255_command.cmd_render_3221a48d.jsdbx" includes="true" />

</j:jelly>

Nothing here is trusted by the server. */ /* One ticked row means "this record": COMMAND analyses the list with that record placed in it (where it sits, and records like it by each of its values). Two or more ticked rows are analysed as exactly that set. Not in the row's own more-actions menu, deliberately. In Service Operations Workspace that menu is built by sn_sow.SOWListTransformSNC, a script in SOW's own scope; the only way to add an item is to edit its customer stub SOWListTransform -- a ServiceNow-owned record -- and it would still only reach SOW. Ticking one row and using this button gives the same result with nothing native touched. */ /* The frame page, not the dashboard: the workspace modal closes when its own iframe navigates, and an analysis navigates on every drill. cmd_frame holds the dashboard in an inner iframe so the modal never sees a reload. */ var PAGE = '/x_2185255_command_cmd_frame.do'; var MAX_CHECKED = 100; /* Every g_list read is guarded. Measured on Australia: on a list with no query at all ("Incidents - All") the list holds query = null, and the platform's own getQuery()/getGroupBy() call .split on it and throw. An empty list query is a legitimate state -- it means "every row" -- so it is read as '' rather than allowed to abort the click. */ function safe(fn, fallback) { try { var v = fn(); return (v === null || v === undefined) ? fallback : v; } catch (e) { return fallback; } } var table = g_list.getTableName(); var fixed = safe(function () { return g_list.getFixedQuery(); }, ''); var query = safe(function () { return g_list.getQuery({ fixed: true }); }, null); if (query === null) { /* getQuery threw: rebuild the same string it would have returned. */ var live = safe(function () { return g_list.query; }, '') || ''; query = [fixed, live].filter(function (s) { return !!s; }).join('^'); } /* getGroupBy() answers with the encoded form ("^GROUPBYpriority"), not the field, so the field is lifted out of it. */ var groupRaw = String(safe(function () { return g_list.getGroupBy(); }, '')); var gm = /GROUPBY([a-z0-9_]+)/.exec(groupRaw); var group = gm ? gm[1] : ''; /* The list definition's own condition ("Open" = active=true) is applied by the list's data broker and is NOT in g_list, which only holds what the viewer changed. '&wlist=' + listId : '') + (group ? '&wgroup=' + encodeURIComponent(group) : '') + (title ? '&wtitle=' + encodeURIComponent(title) : '') + (checked.length === 1 ? <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_script_include"><sys_script_include action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><access>public</access><active>true</active><api_name>x_2185255_command.CmdMeta</api_name><caller_access/><client_callable>false</client_callable><description>COMMAND dashboards. See product/script-includes/CmdMeta.js</description><mobile_callable>false</mobile_callable><name>CmdMeta</name><sandbox_callable>false</sandbox_callable><script><![CDATA[/**
 * CmdMeta. Schema introspection.
 *
 * The product has to work over GRC, ITSM, customer service, HR, projects and
 * assets without a line of per-table configuration, so nothing here may know the
 * name of any table or field. Everything is derived from `sys_dictionary` at
 * request time.
 *
 * That constraint is what makes the thing a product rather than six hard-coded
 * dashboards, and it is also the reason the classification below is careful: a
 * field misclassified here becomes a wrong chart downstream, and the form engine
 * cannot detect the mistake because it only ever sees the classification.
 *
 * Memoised per request. Dictionary reads are cheap individually and there are a
 * lot of them, so each table is described once per page load and reused.
 *
 * ES5 only. Rhino.
 */
var CmdMeta = Class.create();

/* Internal types, grouped by what they mean for charting rather than by what the
   platform calls them. Read `sys_dictionary.internal_type` against these. */
CmdMeta.TYPES = {
    DATE: ['glide_date_time', 'glide_date', 'glide_time', 'due_date',
           'glide_utc_time', 'datetime', 'date'],

    /* Durations are numeric in spirit but need converting before they mean
       anything, so they are tracked separately from plain numbers. */
    DURATION: ['glide_duration', 'timer'],

    NUMBER: ['integer', 'decimal', 'float', 'longint', 'currency', 'price',
             'percent_complete', 'order_index'],

    BOOL: ['boolean'],

    REF: ['reference', 'glide_list', 'document_id', 'domain_id'],

    /* Short strings that are worth grouping by only if their cardinality turns
       out to be low. Decided by measurement, not by type. */
    TEXT: ['string', 'char', 'translated_field', 'translated_text'],

    /* Never a dimension and never a measure. Grouping by a journal or an HTML
       body produces one group per record, which is the failure mode that puts a
       datetime on a scalar tile. */
    OPAQUE: ['journal', 'journal_input', 'journal_list', 'html', 'translated_html',
             'script', 'script_plain', 'script_server', 'xml', 'json', 'sys_class_name',
             'password', 'password2', 'GUID', 'sys_id', 'user_image', 'image',
             'documentation_field', 'conditions', 'glide_var', 'variables',
             'template_value', 'field_name', 'table_name', 'wide_text', 'email_script']
};

/* Fields that are technically groupable and never interesting. Excluded by name
   because their types do not distinguish them from useful fields. */
CmdMeta.NOISE = {
    'sys_id': 1, 'sys_mod_count': 1, 'sys_created_by': 1, 'sys_updated_by': 1,
    'sys_tags': 1, 'sys_domain': 1, 'sys_domain_path': 1, 'sys_class_name': 1,
    'number': 1, 'upon_approval': 1, 'upon_reject': 1, 'order': 1,
    'activity_due': 1, 'wf_activity': 1, 'sys_effective_from': 1,
    'sys_effective_to': 1, 'correlation_id': 1, 'correlation_display': 1
};

/* A cardinality above this and a plain string field is an identifier, not a
   dimension. Applied only to untyped text; choice and reference fields carry
   their own evidence. */
CmdMeta.TEXT_DIM_MAX_DISTINCT = 40;

CmdMeta.prototype = {

    initialize: function () {
        this._tables = {};   // table -> descriptor, memoised per request
        this._fields = {};   // table -> field array
        this._choices = {};  // table|field -> declared choices, in sequence
    },

    /**
     * Describes a table without reading a single row of it.
     *
     * `canRead` is the table-level check. It is necessary and not sufficient:
     * passing it means the viewer may query the table, not that they may see any
     * particular row, which is exactly the distinction that makes
     * GlideAggregate unsafe. Row-level correctness is CmdData's job.
     */
    describe: function (table) {
        if (this._tables[table] !== undefined) return this._tables[table];

        var d = { name: table, label: table, plural: table, exists: false, canRead: false };

        var t = new GlideRecord('sys_db_object');
        t.addQuery('name', table);
        t.setLimit(1);
        t.query();
        if (t.next()) {
            d.exists = true;
            d.label = t.getValue('label') || table;
            d.plural = t.getValue('label') ? (t.getValue('label') + 's') : table;
            d.superClass = t.getDisplayValue('super_class') || '';
        }

        if (d.exists) {
            try {
                d.canRead = new GlideRecord(table).canRead();
            } catch (e) {
                d.canRead = false;
            }
        }

        this._tables[table] = d;
        return d;
    },

    /**
     * Every field on the table, classified. Walks the dictionary including
     * inherited fields, which matters because most of the interesting tables
     * extend `task` and would otherwise appear to have almost no columns.
     */
    fields: function (table) {
        if (this._fields[table] !== undefined) return this._fields[table];

        var out = [];
        var seen = {};

        var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_dictionary');
        gr.addQuery('name', 'IN', this._hierarchy(table).join(','));
        gr.addNotNullQuery('element');
        gr.query();

        while (gr.next()) {
            var el = gr.getValue('element');
            if (!el || seen[el]) continue;
            seen[el] = true;

            var it = gr.getValue('internal_type') || '';
            var f = {
                name: el,
                label: gr.getValue('column_label') || el,
                type: it,
                reference: gr.getValue('reference') || '',
                dependent: gr.getValue('dependent') || '',
                maxLength: parseInt(gr.getValue('max_length'), 10) || 0,
                isDate: this._in(it, CmdMeta.TYPES.DATE),
                isDuration: this._in(it, CmdMeta.TYPES.DURATION),
                isNumber: this._in(it, CmdMeta.TYPES.NUMBER),
                isBool: this._in(it, CmdMeta.TYPES.BOOL),
                isRef: this._in(it, CmdMeta.TYPES.REF),
                isText: this._in(it, CmdMeta.TYPES.TEXT),
                isOpaque: this._in(it, CmdMeta.TYPES.OPAQUE) || !!CmdMeta.NOISE[el]
            };

            /* A choice list is the strongest evidence a field is a dimension:
               somebody has already declared its permitted values. Cheaper to
               read the dictionary flag than to count distinct values. */
            var ch = gr.getValue('choice');
            f.isChoice = (ch === '1' || ch === '2' || ch === '3');

            /* Ordinal means the sequence carries meaning, so the renderer must
               not sort by magnitude. Numeric choice fields are the reliable
               signal here; priority and state are the canonical cases. */
            f.isOrdinal = f.isChoice && (f.isNumber || it === 'integer');

            /* Long free text is never a dimension regardless of type. */
            if (f.isText && f.maxLength > 255) f.isOpaque = true;

            out.push(f);
        }

        out.sort(function (a, b) { return a.label < b.label ? -1 : 1; });
        this._fields[table] = out;
        return out;
    },

    field: function (table, name) {
        var all = this.fields(table);
        for (var i = 0; i < all.length; i++) {
            if (all[i].name === name) return all[i];
        }
        return null;
    },

    /**
     * The declared choices for a field, in the sequence somebody declared them in.
     *
     * Sequence is the point. Everywhere else in this product a value's order comes
     * from measuring the rows, because a declaration records an intention and the
     * rows record a fact. A funnel is the one case where the declared order is the
     * fact being asked about: "does volume shed in the order this field says the
     * work is meant to flow". Without the sequence there is no funnel to test for,
     * only a set of counts.
     *
     * It stays a claim, not a conclusion. CmdAnalysis.funnel() still requires the
     * counts to decline monotonically across this order before it will draw one, so
     * a field whose declared sequence is decorative is rejected on the data.
     */
    choices: function (table, field) {
        var ck = table + '|' + field;
        /* `!== undefined`, not truthiness, and this is not a style preference.
         *
         * An empty array is falsy in the script engine this runs on. Measured on
         * dev390988:
         *
         *     var r = m.choices('incident', 'assigned_to');
         *     r instanceof Array   ->  true
         *     r.length             ->  0
         *     m._choices[ck] !== undefined  ->  true      (it was cached)
         *     !!m._choices[ck]              ->  false     (and the guard missed it)
         *
         * So every field with no declared choices missed the cache on every call
         * and re-queried sys_choice across the whole table hierarchy. That is most
         * fields: a reference, a date and a free-text column all return [].
         *
         * The cost was not small. _canonKey calls this once per field per row, so a
         * reduction over six fields ran at 23.7ms per row against 0.46ms for the
         * bare cursor and 0.36ms for reading all six values. It was 98% of the page
         * scan. One dashboard spent 3.8s to admit fifty rows, exhausted the request
         * allowance, and starved ten further reductions, which is why panels went
         * missing on a page that had already paid for the data.
         *
         * Guarding on presence rather than on truth is correct for any cache whose
         * value may legitimately be empty, zero or false, so every memo in this
         * codebase now does it. */
        if (this._choices[ck] !== undefined) return this._choices[ck];

        /* The most specific table that defines choices for this element wins, and
         * the hierarchy is NOT merged.
         *
         * Merging is what the first version did, and it produced nonsense that was
         * hard to see. `change_request.state` came back as the union of the task
         * base-class vocabulary and the change vocabulary:
         *
         *     Pending 449, Open 0, Assess 314, Work in Progress 0,
         *     Closed Complete 70, Authorize 290, Scheduled 163, ...
         *
         * Two unrelated vocabularies interleaved by a sequence number that only
         * means something within one of them. Every label is real and the order is
         * meaningless, which is the worst combination: the funnel gate rejected it
         * for failing to decline, which was the right answer reached by accident.
         * Had the numbers happened to fall the other way it would have drawn a
         * confident funnel over stages that do not form a sequence.
         *
         * The platform resolves choices by overriding, not by accumulating: a table
         * that declares any choice for an element replaces its parent's list rather
         * than adding to it. This walks the hierarchy from the most specific and
         * takes the first table that declares anything.
         */
        var chain = this._hierarchy(table);
        var out = [];

        for (var h = 0; h < chain.length && !out.length; h++) {
            var seen = {};
            var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_choice');
            gr.addQuery('name', chain[h]);
            gr.addQuery('element', field);
            gr.addQuery('inactive', '!=', true);
            /* Choices are per language; without this a bilingual instance returns
               each value once per installed language and a funnel gets duplicate
               stages. */
            gr.addQuery('language', 'en');
            gr.orderBy('sequence');
            gr.query();
            while (gr.next()) {
                var v = gr.getValue('value');
                if (v === null || v === '' || seen[v]) continue;
                seen[v] = true;
                out.push({
                    value: v,
                    label: gr.getValue('label') || v,
                    sequence: parseInt(gr.getValue('sequence'), 10) || 0,
                    definedOn: chain[h]
                });
            }
        }

        this._choices[ck] = out;
        return out;
    },

    /**
     * Fields worth grouping by, best first.
     *
     * "Best" is a prior, not a decision. It orders the candidates that then get
     * measured; nothing here looks at data. The ordering matters only because
     * measuring every field on a wide table would be slow, so the caller
     * measures down this list and stops when it has enough panels.
     */
    dimensions: function (table) {
        var f = this.fields(table);
        var out = [];

        for (var i = 0; i < f.length; i++) {
            var x = f[i];
            if (x.isOpaque || x.isDate) continue;
            if (!(x.isChoice || x.isBool || x.isRef || x.isText || x.isNumber)) continue;

            /* Plain unbounded text needs its cardinality measured before it can
               be trusted as a dimension. Flagged, not excluded. */
            out.push({
                name: x.name,
                label: x.label,
                type: x.type,
                isChoice: x.isChoice,
                isBool: x.isBool,
                isRef: x.isRef,
                isOrdinal: x.isOrdinal,
                isNumber: x.isNumber,
                needsCardinalityCheck: x.isText && !x.isChoice,
                rank: this._dimRank(x)
            });
        }

        out.sort(function (a, b) { return a.rank - b.rank; });

        /* Interleaved by kind, not returned in strict rank order.
         *
         * Strict rank order puts every ordinal choice field first, and `incident`
         * has six of them, so a caller that examines the first fourteen candidates
         * never reaches `assignment_group` or `category` at all. The downstream
         * panel selection then has nothing diverse to choose between and the page
         * comes out as six variations on one chart.
         *
         * Round-robin across the kinds fixes it at the source: best nominal choice,
         * best ordinal, best reference, best boolean, then the second of each. Rank
         * still decides order within a kind, so the prior is preserved. */
        return this._interleave(out);
    },

    _interleave: function (dims) {
        var buckets = { choice: [], ordinal: [], ref: [], bool: [], other: [] };
        var i;
        for (i = 0; i < dims.length; i++) {
            var d = dims[i];
            if (d.isOrdinal) buckets.ordinal.push(d);
            else if (d.isChoice) buckets.choice.push(d);
            else if (d.isBool) buckets.bool.push(d);
            else if (d.isRef) buckets.ref.push(d);
            else buckets.other.push(d);
        }
        /* Nominal choices lead: a named category is the most legible breakdown a
           viewer can be given, and it is the kind the client's own examples used. */
        var order = ['choice', 'ordinal', 'ref', 'bool', 'other'];
        var out = [], drained = false, round = 0;
        while (!drained && round < 60) {
            drained = true;
            for (i = 0; i < order.length; i++) {
                var b = buckets[order[i]];
                if (round < b.length) { out.push(b[round]); drained = false; }
            }
            round++;
        }
        return out;
    },

    /** Date fields, best first. The one used for a trend defaults to the first. */
    dates: function (table) {
        var f = this.fields(table);
        var out = [];
        for (var i = 0; i < f.length; i++) {
            if (!f[i].isDate || f[i].isOpaque) continue;
            out.push({ name: f[i].name, label: f[i].label, type: f[i].type,
                       rank: this._dateRank(f[i]) });
        }
        out.sort(function (a, b) { return a.rank - b.rank; });
        return out;
    },

    /** Numeric fields that can carry a SUM or an AVG. */
    measures: function (table) {
        var f = this.fields(table);
        var out = [];
        for (var i = 0; i < f.length; i++) {
            var x = f[i];
            if (x.isOpaque) continue;
            if (!x.isNumber && !x.isDuration) continue;
            /* A numeric choice field is an ordinal dimension, not a measure.
               Summing priority produces a number with no meaning. */
            if (x.isChoice) continue;
            out.push({ name: x.name, label: x.label, type: x.type,
                       isDuration: x.isDuration });
        }
        return out;
    },

    /**
     * Declared parent-child field pairs, the dictionary's own hierarchy claim.
     *
     * Returned as candidates only. Measured on this instance,
     * `incident.subcategory` is declared dependent on `category` and is populated
     * on 42 of 13,986 records, so a declaration here means somebody intended a
     * hierarchy and says nothing about whether one exists in the data. CmdDrill
     * gates these on fill rate before any of them reaches a user.
     */
    dependentPairs: function (table) {
        var f = this.fields(table);
        var out = [];
        for (var i = 0; i < f.length; i++) {
            if (!f[i].dependent || f[i].isOpaque) continue;
            var parent = this.field(table, f[i].dependent);
            if (!parent || parent.isOpaque) continue;
            out.push({
                parent: parent.name, parentLabel: parent.label,
                child: f[i].name, childLabel: f[i].label,
                declared: true
            });
        }
        return out;
    },

    /* ── internals ── */

    /** Public name for the inheritance chain. CmdData needs it to find every ACL
        and business rule that could apply to a table, including inherited ones. */
    tableChain: function (table) {
        return this._hierarchy(table);
    },

    /**
     * The table and everything it extends, so inherited columns are found.
     * Without this, `sn_grc_issue` looks like it has six fields.
     */
    _hierarchy: function (table) {
        var chain = [table];
        var cursor = table;
        var guard = 0;
        while (cursor && guard < 12) {
            guard++;
            var t = new GlideRecord('sys_db_object');
            t.addQuery('name', cursor);
            t.setLimit(1);
            t.query();
            if (!t.next()) break;
            var sup = t.getDisplayValue('super_class');
            if (!sup || sup === cursor) break;
            chain.push(sup);
            cursor = sup;
        }
        return chain;
    },

    /* Lower rank sorts first. Ordering is a prior on usefulness: a declared
       choice list beats a reference, which beats a raw string. */
    _dimRank: function (x) {
        if (x.isOrdinal) return 10;
        if (x.isChoice) return 20;
        if (x.isBool) return 30;
        if (x.isRef) return 40;
        if (x.isNumber) return 60;
        return 80;
    },

    /* An opened or created date is what a trend almost always means. A closed or
       resolved date describes only the subset that reached that state, which
       makes it a worse default and a legitimate explicit choice. */
    _dateRank: function (x) {
        var n = x.name;
        if (n === 'opened_at' || n === 'sys_created_on') return 10;
        if (n.indexOf('opened') === 0 || n.indexOf('start') === 0) return 20;
        if (n === 'sys_updated_on') return 70;
        if (n.indexOf('closed') === 0 || n.indexOf('resolved') === 0) return 50;
        if (n.indexOf('due') === 0 || n.indexOf('end') === 0) return 40;
        return 30;
    },

    _in: function (v, arr) {
        for (var i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {
            if (arr[i] === v) return true;
        }
        return false;
    },

    type: 'CmdMeta'
};
]]></script><sys_class_name>sys_script_include</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-07 18:43:05</sys_created_on><sys_id>93a31affc30fcf10f8cef44ed401319d</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>CmdMeta</sys_name><sys_package display_value="COMMAND Analytics" source="x_2185255_command">91bf4637c30fcf10f8cef44ed4013142</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="COMMAND Analytics">91bf4637c30fcf10f8cef44ed4013142</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_script_include_93a31affc30fcf10f8cef44ed401319d</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-07 18:43:05</sys_updated_on></sys_script_include></record_update>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="sys_ui_script"><sys_ui_script action="DELETE"><active>true</active><description>COMMAND dashboards client asset. content hash 2076b25aaa8a</description><global>false</global><ignore_in_now_experience>false</ignore_in_now_experience><name>x_2185255_command.cmd_theme_2076b25aaa8a</name><script><![CDATA[/**
 * cmd_theme. Resolves the theme before anything paints.
 *
 * Loaded first, ahead of the fonts and the renderer, so the correct theme is on the
 * root element before the stylesheet has anything to apply it to. Doing this in the
 * renderer instead would paint light and then repaint dark, which is worse than
 * having no dark theme at all.
 *
 * Light is the default because ServiceNow runs light and this has to belong inside
 * the platform rather than visit it. A stored preference wins, and absent one the
 * operating system's preference is honoured, because a viewer who has told their
 * machine they want dark has already answered the question.
 */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var KEY = 'cmd-theme';

  function stored() {
    try { return window.localStorage.getItem(KEY); } catch (e) { return null; }
  }

  function resolve() {
    var s = stored();
    if (s === 'dark' || s === 'light') return s;
    try {
      if (window.matchMedia &&
          window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches) return 'dark';
    } catch (e) {}
    return 'light';
  }

  function apply(t) {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-cmd-theme', t);
    try { window.localStorage.setItem(KEY, t); } catch (e) {}
  }

  apply(resolve());

  window.CmdTheme = {
    get: function () {
      return document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-cmd-theme') || 'light';
    },
    set: apply,
    toggle: function () {
      var next = this.get() === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark';
      apply(next);
      return next;
    }
  };
})();
]]></script><script_name>cmd_theme_2076b25aaa8a</script_name><sys_class_name>sys_ui_script</sys_class_name><sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-08 06:58:54</sys_created_on><sys_id>0a1cb004c3934350f8cef44ed4013136</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_name>x_2185255_command.cmd_theme_2076b25aaa8a</sys_name><sys_package display_value="COMMAND Analytics" source="x_2185255_command">91bf4637c30fcf10f8cef44ed4013142</sys_package><sys_policy/><sys_scope display_value="COMMAND Analytics">91bf4637c30fcf10f8cef44ed4013142</sys_scope><sys_update_name>sys_ui_script_0a1cb004c3934350f8cef44ed4013136</sys_update_name><sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-08 06:58:54</sys_updated_on><ui_type>0</ui_type><use_scoped_format>false</use_scoped_format></sys_ui_script></record_update>
